analysis.title: Signal over Noise: Finding quality beyond AI
key_insights: UBS CIO introduces 'ARQ' (AI-resilient quality stocks): quality businesses whose models are largely independent of AI, positioned as portfolio ballast alongside AI beneficiaries.

Over the past month semiconductor stocks in the Mag 7 fell 18% versus a 4% decline for the Mag 7 overall, as investors question returns on over USD 4.2 trillion of future spend commitments by US hyperscalers and frontier labs.
Weak momentum in the core business of some digital incumbents in last week's earnings added to concerns about AI-related pressure.

UBS sees continued risk to digital economy stocks: AI agents may take over more digital commerce, questioning advertising efficacy, and AI coding tools make it easier to replace software with cheaper offerings.
The USD 1 trillion advertising market and USD 500 billion software-as-a-service market are described as susceptible to AI disruption.
The quality factor has outperformed world and broader US indices by well over 1% annually over the last 10 years, but those indices include digital incumbents facing AI-native competitors.
UBS suggests overlaying an AI resiliency factor and focusing on businesses tied to basic human needs with toll-taking characteristics, mainly health care and consumer staples.

Health care pick: physical infrastructure and outpatient clinical services (operators of medical centers and rehabilitation facilities), protected by zoning laws and certificate-of-need regulation, with aging demographics as a tailwind and noncyclical revenue.

Consumer staples picks: agricultural processors (ports and mills collecting the spread per metric ton), food distributors (refrigerated truck and hub networks charging a markup), and membership warehouses (sell near cost and earn recurring annual fees).
UBS recommends these AI-resilient quality segments to complement its TRIO portfolios in a diversified equity portfolio.

sector_views.sector: Health care (outpatient clinical services and physical infrastructure)
sector_views.rationale: Local zoning and certificate-of-need rules create localized monopolies, aging demographics support demand, and revenues are noncyclical and insulated from AI replacement risk.

sector_views.sector: Consumer staples (agricultural processors, food distributors, membership warehouses)
sector_views.rationale: Businesses control physical bottlenecks and act as toll-takers, with recurring fees or per-unit spreads that are largely independent of AI.
Exposed to disruption from AI agents in digital commerce and AI coding tools that can replace software with cheaper alternatives.

earnings_insights: Last week's earnings from some digital incumbents showed a lack of momentum in the core business, per UBS, which added to AI-disruption concerns. No specific companies or figures are given.

trade_ideas.description: Add AI-resilient quality (ARQ) segments to diversified equity portfolios: outpatient health care operators, agricultural processors, food distributors, membership warehouses, alongside TRIO portfolios
trade_ideas.rationale: These businesses have physical or regulatory moats and toll-taking characteristics that are largely independent of AI.

risk_factors: AI disruption of digital incumbents via agents in digital commerce and AI coding tools.
Doubts over returns on USD 4.2 trillion of hyperscaler and frontier lab spend commitments pressuring semiconductors.
Quality indices include digital incumbents that face increasing risk from AI-native competitors.
